operations.specification: Guest registration (join) operation for the discussion_board_guests table. This endpoint creates a new guest session for anonymous visitors who want to browse the discussion board. The operation generates a unique session identifier and tracks basic analytics data including IP address, user agent, and visit timestamps. This is a public endpoint that requires no authentication and serves as the entry point for anonymous users to access read-only content on the platform.
operations.description:
Creates a new guest session for unauthenticated visitors to browse the discussion board with read-only access to public content.

This operation registers a new guest user by generating a unique session identifier and capturing essential browsing analytics. The session identifier is stored in the browser to track the guest's activity across visits, enabling analytics on traffic patterns and potential conversion to registered membership. The endpoint collects IP address and user agent information for security monitoring and device analytics while maintaining privacy through anonymous session tracking.

The operation writes to the discussion_board_guests table, creating a record with session_identifier (unique browser-stored token), ip_address (for security monitoring), user_agent (for device analytics), first_visit_at and last_visit_at timestamps (both set to current time), and page_views initialized to zero. All fields are non-nullable as defined in the Prisma schema.

Guests receive JWT tokens upon registration that grant read-only access to published articles, article lists, and public discussions. They cannot create content, comment, upload attachments, or access moderation features. When guests later register as members, this guest record can be linked to track the conversion journey from anonymous browsing to active participation.

Security considerations include rate limiting on guest session creation to prevent abuse, IP-based tracking for security monitoring per the schema's ip_address field, and automatic session expiration based on the last_visit_at timestamp. The unique session_identifier index ensures each guest session is distinct and prevents duplicate session creation.

This is a public endpoint with authorizationActor set to null, as it must be accessible to unauthenticated visitors. The response returns JWT tokens (access and refresh) along with the guest session details, following the IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized response type pattern for authentication operations.

Refreshes JWT access tokens for guest users to maintain continuous browsing sessions and read-only access to discussion board content.

This operation enables guests to renew their authentication tokens using a valid refresh token, extending their session lifetime without interrupting their browsing experience. The endpoint is essential for maintaining seamless access as guests navigate through articles and discussions, automatically handling token expiration in the background.

The operation requires a valid refresh token in the request and updates the discussion_board_guests table by setting last_visit_at to the current timestamp, tracking the guest's ongoing engagement. This timestamp update is crucial for analytics on guest activity patterns, session duration, and engagement frequency as defined in the Prisma schema.

Upon successful token refresh, the endpoint returns new JWT access and refresh tokens along with the guest session details. The page_views counter is not incremented during token refresh (only during actual page navigation), maintaining accurate analytics. Guests retain their read-only permissions, unable to create content, comment, or upload attachments.

Security considerations include validating the refresh token's authenticity and expiration, checking that the guest session still exists and hasn't been invalidated, and updating the last_visit_at field to enable session timeout policies. The unique session_identifier ensures the refresh operation targets the correct guest record.

This endpoint requires a valid refresh token for authorization, so authorizationActor is set to "guest" to ensure only authenticated guest sessions can refresh their tokens. The response follows the IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized pattern, providing fresh tokens and session details to maintain the guest's browsing session.

operations.description:
Registers a new member account for the discussion board platform, enabling users to create and participate in economic and political discussions. This operation creates a new record in the discussion_board_members table with the provided credentials and initiates the email verification process required before full content creation privileges are granted.

The registration process validates that the email and username are unique across all existing members, enforcing the unique constraints defined in the Prisma schema. The password is securely hashed using bcrypt with a work factor of 10+ before storage, ensuring credentials are never stored in plain text. Initial account status sets email_verified to false and is_suspended to false.

Upon successful registration, an email verification token is automatically generated and stored in the discussion_board_email_verifications table with a 24-hour expiration. This token is sent to the member's email address to confirm ownership. Members must complete email verification before they can create articles and access full platform features, as indicated by the email_verified field requirement.

The operation returns JWT tokens (access token with 30-minute expiration and refresh token with 7-day expiration) immediately upon registration, allowing the member to access read-only features and their profile while awaiting email verification. The response includes the member's profile information and verification status.

This operation is public and requires no authentication. It implements the first step in the member lifecycle, followed by email verification (POST /auth/member/email/verify) and eventual login for returning members (POST /auth/member/login).

The session enables stateless JWT authentication with a 30-minute access token and 7-day refresh token. The last_login_at timestamp in the discussion_board_members table is updated to track member activity.

The operation returns JWT tokens along with the member's complete profile information including username, display_name, bio, avatar_url, email verification status (email_verified), and account status. Multiple concurrent sessions are supported, allowing members to access the platform from different devices simultaneously.

This operation is public and requires no prior authentication. It follows member registration (POST /auth/member/join) and email verification (POST /auth/member/email/verify) in the authentication workflow. Refreshes expired or expiring JWT access tokens using a valid refresh token, extending the member's authenticated session without requiring credential re-entry. This operation validates the refresh token against active sessions in the discussion_board_member_sessions table and issues new JWT tokens for continued API access.

The refresh process verifies that the refresh token corresponds to an active session (expired_at is null) and that the associated member account in discussion_board_members is in good standing (not suspended with is_suspended = false, not deleted with deleted_at = null). If the account has been suspended or deleted since the original login, the refresh operation fails and requires re-authentication.

Upon successful validation, new JWT tokens are issued with refreshed expiration times: a 30-minute access token for immediate API requests and a 7-day refresh token for future token renewal. The existing session record in discussion_board_member_sessions remains active, maintaining the original session context including IP address and creation timestamp.

The operation returns the renewed JWT tokens along with the member's current profile information from discussion_board_members, including any updates to username, display_name, bio, avatar_url, and verification status that may have occurred since the original login. This ensures the client application has the latest member data without additional API calls.

This operation requires a valid refresh token but does not require an active access token, enabling seamless token renewal even after access token expiration. It is a critical component of the stateless JWT authentication flow, working in conjunction with login (POST /auth/member/login) to maintain long-lived authenticated sessions across the 30-minute access token expiration boundary.

operations.description:
Verifies a member's email address using the unique verification token sent during registration, enabling full content creation privileges on the discussion board platform. This operation validates the token against discussion_board_email_verifications, confirms it hasn't expired or been used, and updates the member's verification status in discussion_board_members.

Upon successful validation, the operation updates the discussion_board_members table, setting email_verified to true and email_verified_at to the current timestamp for the associated member account. Simultaneously, the verification record in discussion_board_email_verifications is marked as used by setting verified_at to the current timestamp, preventing token reuse.

The email verification requirement gates access to article creation and full platform features. Until email_verified is true, members have limited privileges and cannot create content in the discussion_board_articles table. This security measure ensures account ownership and reduces spam or fraudulent registrations.

This operation is public and requires no authentication, as it's designed to be accessed via email link by users who have just registered but not yet logged in. If the token has expired, members can request a new verification email through a separate endpoint. This operation is a critical intermediate step between registration (POST /auth/member/join) and full platform access.

Accepts member email address, generates a cryptographically secure token, and sends password reset instructions via email.
operations.description:
Initiates a password reset request for a member who has forgotten their password, creating a secure single-use token that enables password change without knowing the current password. This operation creates records in both discussion_board_password_resets and discussion_board_password_reset_of_members tables, following the Compatible Actor Pattern for polymorphic password reset support.

The password reset process begins by validating that the provided email address corresponds to an active member account in discussion_board_members (not deleted with deleted_at = null, not permanently suspended). A cryptographically secure random token is generated and stored in discussion_board_password_resets with actor_type set to 'member', expires_at set to 1 hour from creation, and used_at initially null.

The relationship to the specific member is maintained through discussion_board_password_reset_of_members, which creates a linking record with the discussion_board_password_reset_id and discussion_board_member_id foreign keys. This subtype table enables proper 3NF normalization while supporting password resets for both members and moderators through the same base table.

The generated token is sent to the member's registered email address with instructions to complete the password reset process. The token is valid for 1 hour for security purposes. Members can request multiple password reset emails, with each request creating a new token; however, only unused tokens (used_at is null) can be successfully redeemed.

This operation is public and requires no authentication, as it's specifically designed for users who cannot log in due to forgotten passwords. It's the first step in the password recovery workflow, followed by the password change operation (POST /auth/member/password/reset/complete) which consumes the token and updates the member's password in discussion_board_members.

operations.specification: Password reset completion endpoint that consumes a reset token from discussion_board_password_resets and updates the member's password in discussion_board_members. Validates the token, checks expiration and usage status, updates the password hash, and marks the token as used to prevent reuse.
operations.description:
Completes the password reset process by validating the reset token and updating the member's password in the discussion_board_members table. This operation consumes a single-use token from discussion_board_password_resets, verifies its validity, and securely updates the member's authentication credentials with a new bcrypt-hashed password.

The password reset completion process retrieves the reset record from discussion_board_password_resets using the provided token, validating that actor_type is 'member' and the token hasn't expired (current time < expires_at) or been previously used (used_at is null). The operation then joins to discussion_board_password_reset_of_members to identify the specific member account requiring the password update.

Upon successful token validation, the new password is hashed using bcrypt with work factor 10+ and updates the password field in discussion_board_members for the associated discussion_board_member_id. The password is never stored or transmitted in plain text, maintaining security standards consistent with the initial registration process. The reset token is marked as consumed by setting used_at to the current timestamp in discussion_board_password_resets, preventing token reuse.

As a security measure, all existing sessions in discussion_board_member_sessions for this member are invalidated by setting their expired_at timestamp, forcing re-authentication with the new password across all devices. This prevents unauthorized access if the password reset was initiated maliciously. The member must login again using the new password to create fresh authenticated sessions.

This operation is public and requires no authentication, as it's designed for users who have lost access to their accounts. It completes the password recovery workflow initiated by the password reset request (POST /auth/member/password/reset), restoring account access and requiring fresh login (POST /auth/member/login) with the new credentials.

Validates the current password against discussion_board_members, verifies the member is authenticated, and updates to the new bcrypt-hashed password while invalidating existing sessions except the current one.
operations.description:
Enables authenticated members to change their password as a security maintenance operation, requiring knowledge of the current password to authorize the change. This operation validates the existing password against discussion_board_members, updates to a new bcrypt-hashed password, and manages session lifecycle to maintain security across devices.

The password change process first authenticates the request using the member's JWT access token to identify the discussion_board_member_id. The operation then validates that the provided current password matches the hashed password stored in the discussion_board_members table using bcrypt comparison. This verification prevents unauthorized password changes even if a session token is compromised.

Upon successful current password validation, the new password is hashed using bcrypt with work factor 10+ and updates the password field in discussion_board_members. The password is never stored or transmitted in plain text, consistent with security standards throughout the authentication system. The updated_at timestamp is set to track when the password change occurred.

As a security measure, all existing sessions in discussion_board_member_sessions for this member are invalidated except the current session by setting their expired_at timestamp. This forces re-authentication on other devices while allowing the current session to continue uninterrupted. This prevents potential unauthorized access from previously authenticated devices after a password change.

This operation requires member authentication via JWT access token (authorizationActor: 'member') and differs from the password reset flow which is designed for forgotten passwords. Members use this endpoint for routine password updates or security improvements, maintaining continuous authenticated access throughout the process.

operations.description:
Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of account-level moderation actions from the discussion_board_account_actions table.

This operation provides comprehensive querying capabilities for reviewing the complete history of member account suspensions and bans. Moderators can filter by multiple criteria including the affected member (to view a specific member's disciplinary history), the moderating moderator (to review actions taken by a specific moderator), action type (temporary suspension or permanent ban), current status (active, expired, or reversed), and time period (actions within a specific date range).

Each account action record captures complete context including which member was suspended or banned, which moderator applied the action, the documented reason for the action, the duration (for temporary suspensions), and the current enforcement status. The operation returns paginated results sorted by creation timestamp to show most recent enforcement actions first.

Suspensions are temporary account blocks that prevent members from logging in and creating content for a specified period (1, 7, 14, or 30 days). When the suspension expires, the account is automatically restored to active status. Permanent bans prevent all future access and are reserved for severe or repeated policy violations. Moderators can reverse suspensions and bans if they were applied in error, with all reversals logged for accountability.

This search operation is essential for several moderation workflows: reviewing a specific member's enforcement history before applying escalated discipline, auditing moderator actions to ensure consistent guideline enforcement, generating moderation activity reports for administrative oversight, and identifying patterns of repeat violations that may require permanent bans.

The response includes complete action details, associated member and moderator information, timestamps for all status transitions (created, expired, reversed), and the full audit trail of reasons and reversal justifications. This comprehensive view enables informed moderation decisions based on complete enforcement context.

When invoked, the system creates a new account action record capturing the action type (suspension or ban), the affected member, the moderating moderator (extracted from JWT authentication), the documented reason for enforcement, and the duration for temporary suspensions.

For temporary suspensions, the moderator specifies a duration (1, 7, 14, or 30 days), and the system calculates the expiration timestamp. The member's account status is immediately updated to prevent login and content creation during the suspension period. When the suspension expires, the system automatically restores account access. For permanent bans, no expiration is set, and the member is permanently blocked from all future access.

The operation enforces business rules requiring a documented reason for all enforcement actions to maintain accountability and transparency. The moderator's identity is automatically captured from the authenticated session, creating a complete audit trail. The status is initially set to 'active' for new actions.

This endpoint supports the progressive enforcement model defined in the moderation requirements, where repeated violations lead to escalating consequences (warnings → short suspension → long suspension → permanent ban). Moderators reference the member's violation history before applying enforcement to ensure proportional and consistent discipline.

Upon successful creation, the operation returns the complete account action record including all calculated fields and timestamps. The affected member receives an email notification explaining the action, duration, and reason. Related operations include viewing account actions (GET /accountActions/{actionId}) and searching enforcement history (PATCH /accountActions).

operations.description:
Update the details of an existing account action that was previously applied to a member account. Reversing a suspension or ban immediately restores the member's account access.

The operation validates that the action_type remains consistent (cannot change suspension to ban or vice versa without creating a new action). Status transitions must follow valid state flows (active → reversed, active → expired for suspensions).

Business rules enforced: Duration updates for suspensions must use valid values (1, 7, 14, or 30 days). Reversal operations require both reversal_reason and reversed_by_moderator_id to be set. The expires_at timestamp is recalculated when duration_days is modified. All modifications are logged in the discussion_board_moderation_logs table for comprehensive oversight.

Related operations: This operation works in conjunction with account action creation (POST /accountActions) and retrieval (GET /accountActions/{actionId}). Permanently remove a specific account action record from the system. This operation deletes the historical record of a suspension or ban that was previously applied to a member account. The deletion is permanent and cannot be reversed, removing the action from the member's enforcement history and moderation logs.

The discussion_board_account_actions table maintains a complete audit trail of all account-level moderation actions. Deleting an action record removes it from this history, which may be necessary in cases where an action was created in error, duplicates another record, or needs to be expunged for compliance or privacy reasons. However, deletion should be used sparingly to maintain the integrity of the moderation audit trail.

This operation performs a hard delete, completely removing the record from the database. Unlike reversing an action (which marks it as reversed but preserves the record), deletion eliminates all trace of the action. The member's account status is not directly affected by deleting the action record - if the member is currently suspended or banned, deleting the action record does not automatically restore their access. Account restoration must be handled separately through the update operation with status reversal.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated moderators can delete account action records. The deletion itself is logged in the discussion_board_moderation_logs table with action_type 'account_action_deleted' to maintain accountability. The operation validates that the action exists before attempting deletion and returns appropriate error responses if the action cannot be found.

Business considerations: Deleting active account actions (status = 'active') may leave member accounts in inconsistent states. Best practice is to reverse actions first (using PUT to set status = 'reversed') before deleting the records. This ensures proper account state management and cleaner audit trails. Deletion is primarily intended for cleaning up expired, reversed, or erroneous action records rather than as a primary enforcement tool.

Related operations: Moderators should typically use PUT /accountActions/{actionId} to reverse actions rather than deleting them. Deletion is reserved for administrative cleanup and error correction. The GET /accountActions endpoint can be used to verify action details before deletion. After deletion, the action will no longer appear in the member's enforcement history retrieved via GET /members/{memberId}/accountActions.

Retrieves a paginated list of content reports submitted by members, with advanced filtering and search capabilities for efficient moderation workflow management.

This operation is exclusively available to moderators who need to review community-submitted reports about potentially problematic articles. The endpoint supports comprehensive filtering to help moderators prioritize and manage the moderation queue effectively.

Filtering capabilities include report status (pending, reviewed_no_action, reviewed_edited, reviewed_removed), report category (Spam, Offensive Content, Misinformation, Off-Topic, Other), date ranges for submission time, specific articles being reported, and specific members who submitted reports. Multiple filters can be combined to narrow down results precisely.

The response includes complete report information: reporting member details, reported article summary, selected violation category, optional detailed explanation from the reporter, current resolution status, and resolution details if the report has been reviewed. This comprehensive data enables moderators to understand context and make informed moderation decisions.

Results are paginated with configurable page size (default 20 reports per page) and support sorting by submission date, resolution date, or report priority. Articles with multiple reports are typically prioritized higher in default sorting to surface content requiring urgent attention.

Security: This endpoint requires moderator authentication and authorization. Regular members and guests cannot access content reports. The operation returns reports across all articles regardless of authorship, providing moderators with system-wide visibility.

Related operations: After reviewing reports through this endpoint, moderators typically use article editing operations to modify content, article deletion operations to remove violating content, or report resolution operations to mark reports as reviewed. The moderation workflow integrates tightly with article management operations.

ip_address.description:

Captures the client's browser and device information to enable analytics on device types, browser versions, and platform distribution among guest visitors. This information helps optimize the user experience for the most common browsing environments and identify compatibility issues.

This is a required non-nullable field in the discussion_board_guests table, essential for device analytics and platform optimization.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ICreate.description:
Guest session creation request data for registering anonymous visitors to the discussion board.

This schema defines the data required to create a new guest session, enabling unauthenticated visitors to browse public content with read-only access. The request captures essential session tracking information including a unique session identifier and device information (user_agent and optional ip_address).

The session_identifier is a unique token that will be stored in the browser to maintain continuity across visits and enable conversion tracking when guests later register as members. This field must be unique across all guest sessions as enforced by the database unique constraint.

The ip_address field is optional in the request body since the server can extract it from the HTTP request, but clients may provide it explicitly in server-side rendering scenarios. The user_agent field is required to enable device and browser analytics.

Upon successful guest registration, the system creates a record in the discussion_board_guests table with first_visit_at and last_visit_at timestamps set to the current time, and page_views initialized to zero. id.description:

session_identifier.description:
Unique session identifier for this guest's browsing activity.

The session_identifier from the discussion_board_guests table, provided for client-side storage and tracking. This value should be persisted in the browser (cookie or local storage) to maintain session continuity across page reloads and return visits.

Clients use this identifier to associate page views and browsing behavior with the correct guest session, enabling accurate analytics and session management.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the guest visitor for basic analytics and abuse prevention.

Captured automatically on each visit to support security monitoring, traffic pattern analysis, and geographic distribution insights. Used primarily for identifying suspicious activity patterns, preventing abuse, and understanding visitor geographic origins.

This field contains sensitive data and is restricted to moderator access only. IP addresses are retained for legitimate platform security and analytics purposes in compliance with privacy regulations.

user_agent.description:
Browser user agent string for device and platform analytics.

Contains information about the guest's browser type, version, operating system, and device category. Enables platform administrators to understand visitor device preferences, optimize content delivery for common platforms, and identify compatibility issues.

Typical values include detailed browser signatures like 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36' which can be parsed to extract device type, OS version, and browser details.

first_visit_at.description:
Timestamp of the guest's first visit to the platform.

Recorded when the guest session is initially created, this timestamp marks the beginning of the guest's journey on the platform. Used to calculate visitor recency metrics, analyze new visitor acquisition patterns, and track conversion timelines from first visit to potential member registration.

Stored in ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone for consistent temporal analysis across different geographic regions.

last_visit_at.description:
Timestamp of the guest's most recent activity.

Reflects the updated last_visit_at value from the discussion_board_guests table after the refresh operation. This timestamp is set to the current moment when tokens are refreshed, indicating the guest's ongoing engagement.

Clients can display this value to show session age or use it for local session timeout logic coordinated with the server's expiration policies.

page_views.description:

Incremented on each page navigation to track cumulative engagement level. High page view counts indicate highly engaged visitors who may be strong conversion candidates for member registration.

updated_at.description:

Automatically updated whenever any field in the guest record changes, typically on each new visit when last_visit_at and page_views are incremented. Used for tracking record freshness and data synchronization.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized.description:

Returned when a guest successfully refreshes their authentication tokens, providing new credentials and updated session information. This response enables the client to continue the guest's browsing session with fresh tokens, maintaining read-only access to discussion board content.

The response includes the guest's unique identifier, complete JWT token set (access and refresh tokens), session identifier for client-side tracking, and the updated last_visit_at timestamp reflecting the current engagement. These elements together provide everything needed to maintain stateless authentication and accurate session tracking.

Guests receive this response structure after token refresh operations, with the last_visit_at field updated to the current timestamp to record ongoing activity. The tokens contain claims specific to guest permissions (read-only access, no content creation rights), enforcing proper authorization boundaries throughout the application.

refresh_token.description:

The refresh token issued during the initial guest session creation, used to obtain new access tokens without re-establishing the session. This token has a longer expiration period (typically 7-30 days) compared to access tokens and must be kept secure in the client application.

The refresh token contains the guest's session_identifier claim, enabling the server to locate the corresponding discussion_board_guests record and verify the session is still active and valid. Refresh tokens are single-use and invalidated after successful refresh to prevent replay attacks.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRefresh.description:

The request contains only the refresh token, which the server validates against active guest sessions. Upon successful validation, the server generates new access and refresh tokens, updates the guest's last_visit_at timestamp to reflect the ongoing engagement, and returns the updated credentials.

This operation is essential for seamless user experience, preventing interruptions in browsing when tokens expire. It enables long-term guest sessions while maintaining security through periodic token rotation.

The id field identifies the authenticated member from discussion_board_members table. The token field contains the access token (for API requests) and refresh token (for token renewal). This response type is used for login operations (POST /auth/member/login) and email verification with auto-login (POST /auth/member/email/verify). After receiving this response, clients store the tokens and include the access_token in the Authorization header for all subsequent protected requests.

This DTO contains the verification token that members receive in their registration email. The token is validated against discussion_board_email_verifications table to confirm it exists, hasn't expired (created_at + 24 hours > current time), and hasn't been used (verified_at is null).

Successful verification updates the discussion_board_members table, setting email_verified to true and email_verified_at to current timestamp. This gates access to article creation and full platform features. The verification record in discussion_board_email_verifications is marked as used by setting verified_at timestamp.

This is a public operation requiring no authentication, as it's designed for newly registered users who haven't logged in yet. The token itself serves as the authorization mechanism, proving the user has access to the registered email address.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequestPasswordR.description:
Request body for initiating a member password reset process.

This DTO contains the member's email address to identify the account requiring password recovery. The backend validates that the email corresponds to an active member account (not deleted, not permanently suspended) before generating a cryptographically secure reset token.

The email is used to look up the member in the discussion_board_members table and create corresponding records in discussion_board_password_resets (with actor_type='member') and discussion_board_password_reset_of_members tables following the Compatible Actor Pattern.

This is a public operation requiring no authentication, as it's designed for users who cannot log in. The reset token is sent to the provided email address with expiration set to 1 hour from creation.

email.description:
Member's registered email address for password reset.

Must match an existing email in the discussion_board_members table. Used to identify the member account and deliver the password reset token. The email lookup validates that the account is active (deleted_at is null and not permanently suspended).

The reset instructions and secure token will be sent to this email address. Case-insensitive comparison is used for email matching to handle user input variations.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordResetReq.description:
Response confirming successful password reset request creation.

This DTO provides confirmation that a password reset token has been generated and sent to the member's email address. It includes the token expiration information to inform the user of the time window for completing the reset process.

The response confirms that records were created in discussion_board_password_resets and discussion_board_password_reset_of_members tables. The token is valid for 1 hour from creation and can be used once to set a new password via the password reset completion endpoint.

message.description:
Confirmation message indicating the password reset email has been sent.

Provides user-friendly feedback that the reset process has been initiated successfully. Typical message: 'Password reset instructions have been sent to your email address.'

For security purposes, this message is shown even if the email doesn't exist in the system, preventing email enumeration attacks.

expires_in_minutes.description:
Number of minutes until the reset token expires.

Indicates the time window (typically 60 minutes) during which the member must use the reset token to complete the password change. After expiration, a new reset request must be initiated.

This value corresponds to the difference between expires_at and created_at in the discussion_board_password_resets record.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for public profile.

If not set, username is used for display. Can be updated by member to provide a more personalized public identity. Must follow same length constraints as username (3-30 characters) when provided.

bio.description:
Optional member biography or description for public profile.

Maximum 500 characters. Allows members to introduce themselves and share their background or interests. Can be set to null to clear existing biography.

avatar_url.description:
URL to profile avatar image.

Must be valid JPEG or PNG format, resized to 200x200 pixels. Can be set to null to remove avatar. Must be a valid URI pointing to the stored image resource.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate.description:
Member profile update request for modifying editable account information.

Contains only the profile fields that members can update through the profile edit interface. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates of specific profile attributes without requiring complete data submission.

Authentication fields (email, password, username) are excluded as they require separate verification workflows to maintain account security. System-managed fields (timestamps, verification status, suspension controls) are also excluded as they are controlled by system processes or moderator actions.

The member's updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time when any changes are saved. Members can only update their own profiles unless they have moderator privileges.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the member.

Primary key used to reference this member across the system. Generated automatically on member registration.

username.description:
Unique display name chosen by the member.

Used for member identification in articles, comments, and discussions. Must be unique across all members to prevent confusion and ensure clear attribution.

display_name.description:
Optional full name or preferred display name.

If provided, shown alongside username in member profiles and article bylines. Allows members to use a more formal or complete name than their username. May be null if member prefers username-only display.

IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary.description:
Essential member information for author attribution and references.

Provides minimal member details needed for displaying article authors, content creators, and participant identification. Used when showing member context in article listings, comments, and activity feeds without loading full member profiles.

token.description:
Password reset token from discussion_board_password_resets table. This single-use token was generated during the password reset request (POST /auth/member/password/reset) and sent to the member's email address.

The token is validated to ensure it exists in discussion_board_password_resets with actor_type='member', hasn't expired (current time < expires_at), and hasn't been previously used (used_at is null). Upon successful password update, this token is marked as consumed to prevent reuse attacks.

password.description:
New password for the member account in plain text. This password will be hashed using bcrypt with work factor 10+ before being stored in the discussion_board_members table's password field.

The password is never stored or transmitted in plain text form in the database. After hashing, it replaces the existing password hash for the member identified through the discussion_board_password_reset_of_members relationship. All existing sessions are invalidated after the password update for security.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IResetPassword.description:
Request body for completing the password reset process for a discussion board member.

This DTO contains the password reset token that was sent to the member's email and the new password they wish to set. The token uniquely identifies the password reset request in discussion_board_password_resets and links to the specific member account through discussion_board_password_reset_of_members.

The operation validates the token's authenticity, expiration status, and single-use constraint before updating the member's password hash in discussion_board_members. This is a public endpoint requiring no authentication, as it's designed for members who have lost access to their accounts.

Upon successful completion, all existing sessions in discussion_board_member_sessions are invalidated, forcing the member to login again with the new password. This prevents unauthorized access if the password reset was initiated maliciously.

success.description: Indicates whether the password reset completion was successful. Always true when the operation completes without errors, confirming that the new password has been set and all existing sessions have been invalidated.

message.description: Human-readable confirmation message indicating successful password reset completion. Typically informs the member that their password has been updated and they need to login again with the new credentials.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordResetCom.description:
Response confirming successful password reset completion for a discussion board member.

This response is returned after the password reset token has been validated, the member's password in discussion_board_members has been updated with the new bcrypt-hashed password, and all existing sessions have been invalidated. The member must now login again using the new password to create a fresh authenticated session.

The success field confirms the operation completed successfully, while the message provides user-friendly confirmation text. This response indicates that the single-use token from discussion_board_password_resets has been consumed (used_at set) and cannot be reused for security purposes.

message.description:
Confirmation message indicating successful password change.

Provides user-facing feedback that the password update operation completed successfully and existing sessions have been invalidated for security.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IPasswordChanged.description:
Password change confirmation response for authenticated members.

Returned after successful password update operation to confirm that the member's password has been changed in the discussion_board_members table and existing sessions have been invalidated. This response provides user-facing feedback without exposing sensitive authentication details.

The response indicates that the password change completed successfully, the new bcrypt-hashed password is stored in discussion_board_members, and all other sessions except the current one have been invalidated for security purposes. The member can continue using their current session while other devices will require re-authentication.

currentPassword.description:
The member's current password in plain text for verification. This password is validated against the hashed password stored in the discussion_board_members table using bcrypt comparison.

This verification step is critical for security - it prevents unauthorized password changes even if a session token is compromised. The current password must match the existing password hash in the database for the authenticated member before the new password is accepted.

The password is never stored or transmitted in plain text form in the database. It is only used for verification during this operation.

newPassword.description:
The new password for the member account in plain text. This password will be hashed using bcrypt with work factor 10+ before being stored in the discussion_board_members table's password field, replacing the current password hash.

The password is never stored or transmitted in plain text form in the database. After successful validation of the current password and hashing of the new password, the updated password hash replaces the existing one for the authenticated member.

All existing sessions except the current one are invalidated in discussion_board_member_sessions after the password update for security purposes.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IChangePassword.description:
Request body for changing the password of an authenticated discussion board member.

This DTO contains both the current password for verification and the new password to set. The member must be authenticated via JWT access token (authorizationActor: 'member'), and the discussion_board_member_id is extracted from the token rather than the request body.

The operation first validates that the currentPassword matches the existing bcrypt-hashed password in discussion_board_members. This verification prevents unauthorized password changes even if a session token is compromised. Upon successful validation, the newPassword is bcrypt-hashed and updates the password field in discussion_board_members.

After the password update, all existing sessions in discussion_board_member_sessions for this member are invalidated except the current session, forcing re-authentication on other devices while maintaining the current session. The updated_at timestamp is set to track when the password change occurred.

This endpoint differs from password reset (which requires no authentication) and is designed for routine password updates or security improvements by authenticated members.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ICreate.description:
Moderator registration request containing credentials and profile information.

Provides all necessary data for creating a new moderator account in the discussion_board_moderators table. The password is transmitted in plain text over HTTPS and will be hashed using bcrypt (work factor 10+) before storage.

Email and username must be unique across all moderators. The display_name is optional and can be set later. The email_verified field will be set to false initially, requiring email verification before granting full moderation privileges.

Includes session context fields (ip, href, referrer) for creating the initial moderator session in discussion_board_moderator_sessions, enabling immediate authenticated access after successful registration.

email.description: Moderator's email address. Must be unique across all moderator accounts. Used for authentication and communication

password.description: Moderator's password in plain text. Will be hashed using bcrypt with work factor 10+ before storage. Must meet security requirements

username.description: Moderator's unique username for identification within the platform. Must be unique across all moderator accounts

display_name.description: Optional display name for the moderator. Can be different from username and may include spaces or special characters

ip.description: Client IP address for initial session creation and security auditing. Server can extract this from request headers, but client may provide for SSR scenarios

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where the registration is occurring. Used for initial session tracking

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) before registration. Used for initial session context. Can be empty string for direct navigation

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized.description:
Response body containing moderator profile and JWT authentication tokens after successful login or token refresh.

This DTO represents a successfully authenticated moderator session, providing both the moderator's identity information and the JWT tokens needed for subsequent authenticated API requests. It is returned from login operations and token refresh operations.

The response includes comprehensive moderator profile information for client-side state management and display purposes. All sensitive fields (password, hashed credentials) are excluded from this response type following security best practices.

The token object contains both access and refresh tokens with their respective expiration periods. Access tokens expire after 30 minutes and must be included in the Authorization header for authenticated requests. Refresh tokens expire after 7 days and are used to obtain new access tokens without re-authentication.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated moderator account.

This UUID corresponds to the discussion_board_moderators.id primary key and uniquely identifies the moderator across the system. It is used for relating moderation actions, session management, and audit trail tracking.

email.description:
Verified email address of the authenticated moderator.

This email is used for moderator authentication, communication, and account recovery. It is guaranteed to be unique across all moderators and verified (email_verified=true) before moderation privileges are granted.

username.description:
Unique username identifying the moderator in moderation logs and actions.

This username is displayed when the moderator edits or moderates content, providing transparency about which moderator performed specific moderation actions. It must be unique across all moderators.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for moderator profile presentation.

If set, this display name is used for moderator profile display instead of the username. If null, the username serves as the display name. This allows moderators to have a more formal or preferred name for public-facing moderation activities.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the moderator's email address has been verified.

This must be true for moderators to exercise their moderation privileges. Email verification is required to ensure moderators can receive important account notifications and security alerts.

email_verified_at.description:
Timestamp when email verification was completed for this moderator account.

Records the exact moment when the moderator completed email verification. Null until verification is completed. Used for audit trails and security monitoring.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether the moderator account is currently active and can perform moderation actions.

Inactive moderators (is_active=false) cannot login or perform any moderation operations. This flag allows system administrators to temporarily suspend moderator privileges without deleting the account.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the moderator's most recent successful login before this session.

This is updated each time the moderator successfully authenticates. It is used for activity tracking, security monitoring, and detecting unusual login patterns. Null for first-time login.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was created by system administrator.

This records when the moderator was granted moderation privileges. Moderator accounts are created by administrators, not through self-registration.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was last updated.

Automatically updated whenever any field in the moderator account is modified. Used for tracking account modifications and synchronization purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when moderator privileges were revoked and account deleted. Supports soft deletion for audit trail.

Implements soft deletion for moderator accounts. When set to a timestamp value, the account is considered deleted and the moderator loses all privileges. Null for active accounts. Preserves account records for accountability and audit purposes even after deletion.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ILogin.description:
Moderator login credentials for authentication.

Provides email and password for validating moderator identity against the discussion_board_moderators table. The password is transmitted in plain text over HTTPS and verified against the bcrypt hash stored in the database.

Additionally includes session context fields (ip, href, referrer) that are captured during the login process to create an audit trail in discussion_board_moderator_sessions. These fields enable security monitoring and help trace moderation actions back to specific login sessions.

Only active moderators (is_active=true) with non-deleted accounts (deleted_at=null) can successfully authenticate.

email.description: Moderator's email address registered in the system. Must match an existing moderator account in discussion_board_moderators table

password.description: Moderator's password in plain text for verification against the bcrypt hash stored in the database. Transmitted securely over HTTPS

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing. Server can extract this from request headers, but client may provide for SSR scenarios

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where the login is occurring. Used for session tracking and security auditing

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) before login. Used for session context tracking. Can be empty string for direct navigation

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing moderator access tokens using a valid refresh token.

This DTO enables moderators to extend their authenticated session without re-entering credentials. When the 30-minute access token expires, moderators use their 7-day refresh token to obtain new JWT tokens, maintaining session continuity seamlessly.

The refresh token is validated against active moderator sessions (discussion_board_moderator_sessions with null expired_at) belonging to active moderators (is_active=true, deleted_at=null). Only valid, non-expired refresh tokens from active sessions can successfully generate new access tokens.

This operation does not require session context fields (ip, href, referrer) because it reuses an existing session rather than creating a new one. The refresh token itself contains the session context from the original login.

refresh_token.description:
Valid refresh token from moderator's current session for generating new access token.

This JWT refresh token was issued during the moderator's initial login or previous token refresh. It has a 7-day validity period and is used to authenticate the refresh request without requiring password re-entry.

The token is validated against the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table to ensure it belongs to an active session (expired_at is null) and an active moderator account (is_active=true, deleted_at=null). Expired or invalid tokens result in authentication failure requiring fresh login.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRequestPasswo.description:
Request body for initiating moderator password reset process by email.

This DTO enables moderators who have forgotten their password to securely recover their account. The moderator provides their registered email address, and the system generates a cryptographically secure reset token sent to that email, allowing password recovery without current password knowledge.

The operation creates a password reset record in discussion_board_password_resets with actor_type='moderator' and a 1-hour expiration period. A corresponding entry is created in discussion_board_password_reset_of_moderators to link the reset request to the specific moderator account, following the Compatible Actor Pattern for proper 3NF normalization.

For security, the system validates that the email belongs to an active moderator (is_active=true, deleted_at=null) but returns success regardless of whether the email exists, preventing account enumeration attacks. Reset tokens are single-use and invalidated after successful password change or expiration.

email.description:
Registered email address of the moderator account requesting password reset.

This must match the email stored in discussion_board_moderators.email for the password reset to be processed. The system validates that this email belongs to an active moderator account before generating the reset token.

The reset token will be sent to this email address, allowing the moderator to click a secure reset link and set a new password. For security, the response does not reveal whether the email exists in the system, preventing account enumeration.

token.description:
Password reset token received via email.

Unique identifier linking to the password reset request in the discussion_board_password_resets table. This token is generated when a moderator requests password reset through the password reset request endpoint and sent to their registered email address.

The token must be valid (not expired, not previously used) and must belong to an active moderator account. The system validates this token against discussion_board_password_resets where actor_type='moderator', used_at=null, and expires_at > current time.

The token is linked to the moderator account through the discussion_board_password_reset_of_moderators relationship table, which contains the discussion_board_moderator_id. Once used successfully, the used_at timestamp is set, making the token invalid for future use.

password.description:
New password for the moderator account.

Plain text password that will replace the current password in the discussion_board_moderators table. The password must meet minimum security requirements including minimum length of 8 characters and complexity standards.

The backend hashes this password using bcrypt with work factor 10+ before storing it in the password_hashed column of the discussion_board_moderators table. The plain text password is never stored in the database.

After successful password reset, the moderator can use this new password with their email address to authenticate through the standard moderator login endpoint.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IResetPassword.description:
Request body for moderator password reset confirmation.

Contains the reset token and new password required to complete the password reset process. This DTO is used when a moderator submits the password reset form after receiving the reset token via email.

The operation validates the token, ensures it belongs to an active moderator account, hasn't expired or been used, and then updates the moderator's password in the discussion_board_moderators table. The token is marked as used after successful password reset to prevent reuse.

This is a public operation (no authentication required) since moderators who forgot their password cannot authenticate. Security is ensured through the cryptographically secure reset token validation.

token.description:
Email verification token received via email.

Unique identifier linking to the email verification request in the discussion_board_email_verifications table. This token is generated when a moderator account is created or when email verification is re-requested, and sent to the moderator's registered email address.

The token must be valid (not expired, not previously verified) and must belong to the authenticated moderator. The system validates this token against discussion_board_email_verifications where discussion_board_member_id matches the authenticated moderator's ID, verified_at=null, and expires_at > current time.

Upon successful verification, the verified_at timestamp in the email verification record is set, and the moderator's email_verified status in discussion_board_moderators table is updated to true with email_verified_at timestamp. The token becomes invalid after successful verification to prevent reuse.

Email verification is required for moderators to access full moderation capabilities. Moderators with unverified emails may have restricted access to certain moderation features.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IVerifyEmail.description:
Request body for moderator email verification confirmation.

Contains the verification token required to confirm the moderator's email address. This DTO is used when an authenticated moderator submits the email verification form after receiving the verification token via email.

The operation validates the token belongs to the authenticated moderator (authorizationActor='moderator'), hasn't expired, and hasn't been used previously. Upon successful validation, the discussion_board_moderators table is updated with email_verified=true and email_verified_at timestamp.

This is an authenticated operation requiring the moderator to be logged in, ensuring only the account owner can verify their own email address. The token validation and email verification status update occur within a single database transaction to maintain data consistency.

Email verification is a security measure to confirm the moderator owns the email address associated with their account and is required before full moderation privileges are granted.

currentPassword.description:
Current password for validation. Must match the moderator's existing password hash in the database.

This field is required for security validation before allowing password change. The backend will compare this value against the stored bcrypt hash to verify the moderator's identity and authorization to change the password.

The password is transmitted in plain text over HTTPS and immediately hashed for comparison - it is never stored in plain text.

newPassword.description:
New password to set for the moderator account. Must meet security requirements.

The new password must be at least 8 characters long and should contain a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters for security. The backend will hash this password using bcrypt with work factor 10+ before storing it in the discussion_board_moderators table.

The new password must be different from the current password to prevent accidental no-change updates.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IChangePasswor.description:
Password change request for authenticated moderators.

This DTO contains the current password for validation and the new password to be set. Unlike password reset flows that use email tokens, this password change operation requires the moderator to provide their current password for security validation.

The current password is verified against the stored bcrypt hash before allowing the password change to proceed. This prevents unauthorized password changes even if an authenticated session is compromised.

After successful password change, existing moderator sessions may be invalidated to force re-authentication with the new password for enhanced security.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Starts at 1 for the first page.

Used to navigate through paginated results when the total number of members exceeds the limit per page. Increment this value to retrieve subsequent pages of results.

limit.description:
Number of members to return per page. Maximum 100 items per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Larger values return more results per request but may impact performance. The maximum limit of 100 prevents excessive data transfer and ensures reasonable response times.

search.description:
Text search query for finding members by username or display name.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching against the username and display_name fields in the discussion_board_members table. Returns members whose username or display name contains the search term.

Example: Searching for 'john' would match usernames like 'john_doe', 'johnsmith', or display names like 'John Anderson'.

emailVerified.description:
Filter by email verification status.

When true, returns only members whose email address has been verified (email_verified = true). When false, returns only members with unverified email addresses. When omitted, returns all members regardless of verification status.

Email verification is required before members can create articles and access full platform features.

isSuspended.description:
Filter by account suspension status.

When true, returns only suspended members (is_suspended = true). When false, returns only active members who are not suspended. When omitted, returns all members regardless of suspension status.

Suspended members cannot login or create content until the suspension expires or is lifted by moderators.

createdAfter.description:
Filter members registered after this timestamp.

Returns only members whose created_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this value. Use ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z').

Useful for finding recently registered members or analyzing member growth within specific time periods.

createdBefore.description:
Filter members registered before this timestamp.

Returns only members whose created_at timestamp is less than or equal to this value. Use ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z').

Combine with createdAfter to define a specific registration date range for analysis.

lastLoginAfter.description:
Filter members who logged in after this timestamp.

Returns only members whose last_login_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this value. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

Useful for identifying recently active members or filtering out inactive accounts.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by.

Determines which field is used for ordering the member list. Options are:
- 'created_at': Sort by registration date (default)
- 'last_login_at': Sort by most recent login activity
- 'username': Sort alphabetically by username

Combine with orderDirection to control ascending or descending order.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for retrieving paginated member lists.

This DTO provides comprehensive filtering and searching capabilities for querying the discussion_board_members table. All filter parameters are optional, allowing flexible queries from simple pagination to complex multi-criteria searches.

The search parameter performs text matching across username and display_name fields, enabling member discovery by partial name matching. Status filters (emailVerified, isSuspended) allow moderators to identify members in specific account states for administrative actions.

Date range filters (createdAfter, createdBefore, lastLoginAfter) support temporal analysis of member registration and activity patterns. These filters can be combined to answer questions like 'How many members registered last month?' or 'Which members haven't logged in for 90 days?'

Pagination is controlled through page and limit parameters, with a maximum limit of 100 items per page to ensure reasonable response times and prevent excessive data transfer.

Results can be sorted by registration date, last login activity, or username, with configurable ascending or descending order. Default ordering is by created_at descending, showing newest members first.

id.description:
Primary identifier for the article category.

Unique identifier used to reference this category in article creation and filtering operations. Generated automatically by the system upon category creation.

name.description:
Category display name shown to users.

Examples include 'Economic Discussion', 'Political Discussion', 'General Discussion'. This is the primary label users see when browsing categories or creating articles.

Must be unique across all categories to prevent confusion and ensure clear category identification.

slug.description:
URL-friendly category identifier derived from name.

Used in category filter URLs and routing to create clean, readable URLs. Must be unique and lowercase with hyphens replacing spaces.

Example: 'Economic Discussion' becomes 'economic-discussion'.

description.description:
Optional explanation of what types of articles belong in this category.

Helps members choose the appropriate category when creating articles by providing guidance on topic scope and expected content.

Can include topic guidelines, example subjects, and clarification of category boundaries to improve content organization.

sort_order.description:
Display order for category lists.

Lower numbers appear first in category selection dropdowns and category browsing interfaces. Allows administrators to prioritize category presentation based on importance or popularity.

Typically sequential integers starting from 1.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this category was created by administrators.

Used for category management audit trails and tracking the evolution of the category taxonomy over time.

Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when category details were last modified.

Updated whenever administrators edit category information including name, description, or sort order. Enables tracking of category definition changes.

Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.description:
Predefined discussion category for organizing articles by topic area.

Represents one of the available category options (Economic Discussion, Political Discussion, General Discussion) that members select when creating articles. Categories help users discover relevant discussions and browse articles by topic focus.

Each category has a unique name and optional description explaining the types of discussions that belong to it. Categories are managed by administrators and provide the organizational taxonomy for the entire discussion board.

id.description:
Primary identifier for the article category.

Unique identifier used to reference this category in article creation and filtering operations. Generated automatically upon category creation using UUID v4 format.

name.description:
Category display name shown to users.

The primary label users see when browsing categories or creating articles. Examples include 'Economic Discussion', 'Political Discussion', 'General Discussion'. Must be unique across all categories to prevent confusion and ensure clear topic identification.

slug.description:
URL-friendly category identifier derived from name.

Used in category filter URLs and routing. Must be unique and lowercase with hyphens, for example 'economic-discussion' or 'political-discussion'. Automatically generated from the category name during creation.

description.description:
Optional explanation of what types of articles belong in this category.

Helps members choose the appropriate category when creating articles. Can include topic guidelines, examples of suitable discussions, and scope clarifications. May be null if the category name is self-explanatory.

sort_order.description:
Display order for category lists.

title.description:

slug.description:

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:

Members can create unlimited articles, edit their own articles at any time, and delete their own content. Moderators have elevated permissions to edit any article for quality control or delete articles that violate community guidelines. Articles support rich text formatting and track engagement through view counts.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for article discovery.

Provides comprehensive querying capabilities for finding discussion articles based on multiple criteria including text search, category filtering, publication status, author identification, date ranges, and popularity metrics. All parameters are optional, enabling flexible search from broad queries to highly specific filters.

Supports pagination through page and limit parameters for efficient navigation through large result sets. Text search leverages full-text indexes on title and body fields for fast keyword discovery. Sorting options enable various discovery patterns from newest content to most popular discussions.

Visibility rules are enforced based on authentication: guest users see only published articles, members see published articles plus their own drafts, and moderators can search all statuses. The status filter interacts with authorization to ensure proper content access control.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.description:
Complete authentication session entity for discussion board members.

Represents an active or expired authentication session associated with a member account, tracking secure stateless authentication via JWT tokens. Each session record captures the authentication lifecycle including creation timestamp, optional expiration timestamp, and connection context metadata such as IP address, referrer URL, and access location.

Sessions are created during member login operations and remain active until explicitly terminated by logout, forceful session revocation by moderators, or natural expiration. The session entity maintains a foreign key relationship to the discussion_board_members table via discussion_board_member_id, establishing ownership of the session.

Connection context fields (ip, href, referrer) provide security monitoring capabilities, enabling detection of suspicious authentication patterns, geographic anomalies, and unauthorized access attempts. These fields are captured at session creation time and remain immutable throughout the session lifecycle.

This type is used in session detail retrieval responses, session termination responses, and anywhere complete session information with full metadata is required. For list views and embedded references, use IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.ISummary instead to reduce payload size.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the authentication session.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the session record and is used in session management operations such as session termination (DELETE /sessions/{sessionId}). The session ID is included in JWT tokens to link authentication credentials to specific session records, enabling session-level token revocation.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the member who owns this authentication session.

This field establishes the ownership relationship between sessions and member accounts. It is used to filter sessions by member (e.g., retrieving all sessions for a specific member), enforce authorization rules (members can only view/delete their own sessions), and maintain referential integrity with the discussion_board_members table.

Note: This raw FK is included for referential integrity documentation. The 'member' field provides the transformed object reference with complete member context.

member.description:
Member who owns this authentication session.

Provides complete member identification and context for this session, enabling clients to display member information without additional API calls. This transformed reference replaces the need to fetch member details separately using discussion_board_member_id.

The member reference is essential for session management interfaces, security dashboards, and audit logs where understanding session ownership and member identity is critical for security monitoring and access control decisions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the authentication session was created (ISO 8601 format).

Records the exact moment when the member successfully authenticated and the session was established. This timestamp is used to calculate session duration, sort sessions chronologically, filter by creation date ranges, and detect rapid session creation patterns that might indicate credential stuffing attacks.

The created_at value is immutable and set automatically by the system during session creation - it cannot be modified after the session is established.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expired or was terminated (ISO 8601 format), or null if still active.

For active sessions, this field is null indicating the session remains valid. When a session expires naturally, is explicitly terminated via logout, or is forcefully revoked by moderators, this field is set to the termination timestamp. The expired_at value provides an audit trail of session lifecycle and enables filtering between active and expired sessions.

Sessions with non-null expired_at values are considered invalid for authentication purposes - any authentication attempts using tokens from expired sessions are rejected with 401 Unauthorized.

ip.description:
IP address of the client when the session was created.

Records the network address from which the authentication request originated. This field supports security monitoring by enabling detection of geographic anomalies (e.g., rapid logins from different countries), IP-based session filtering, and forensic investigation of suspicious authentication patterns.

The IP address is captured at session creation time and remains immutable. Stored as a string to support both IPv4 and IPv6 formats.

href.description:
The URL of the page where the authentication request originated (connection URL).

Captures the exact location in the application from which the member initiated the login process. This field helps understand user authentication patterns, identify authentication entry points, and detect anomalous authentication attempts from unexpected URLs that might indicate phishing or session hijacking.

The href value is provided by the client during authentication and represents the current page URL at the moment of login. It is required and immutable after session creation.

referrer.description:
The URL of the page that referred to the authentication page (referrer URL).

Records the previous page the member was visiting before they initiated the login process. This field provides context about user navigation flows, helps identify authentication sources (e.g., came from article page, came from external site), and can detect suspicious referrer patterns that might indicate phishing attempts.

The referrer value is provided by the client during authentication based on the browser's document.referrer property. It is required and immutable after session creation. May be an empty string if the member navigated directly to the login page.

Records the IP address from which this session was initiated. Used for security monitoring, abuse detection, and geographic analysis of member activity.
