Represents a member's authenticated connection enabling secure stateless authentication with JWT tokens. Sessions track connection context for security monitoring and support multiple concurrent sessions across different devices.

IDiscussionBoardMemberSession.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for retrieving member authentication sessions.

Defines the query criteria used when requesting paginated lists of member sessions through operations like PATCH /members/{memberId}/sessions or PATCH /my/sessions. Supports filtering by session status (active vs expired), creation date ranges, IP address patterns, and connection context, along with sorting and pagination controls.

This request DTO enables security monitoring use cases such as identifying all active sessions for session management, finding sessions from specific IP ranges for geographic analysis, detecting rapid session creation patterns, and reviewing historical authentication activity. All filter criteria are optional, allowing flexible querying from broad session lists to highly specific searches.

Pagination parameters (page, limit) control result set size and navigation through large session collections. Sorting options enable chronological ordering by creation date, expiration date, or other session attributes to support various monitoring and management workflows.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve from the total result set. For example, page=1 returns the first page, page=2 returns the second page. Combined with 'limit' to calculate offset for database queries.

Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return per page.

Controls the result set size for pagination. For example, limit=20 returns up to 20 sessions per page. The system enforces a maximum limit of 100 to prevent excessive payload sizes and maintain API performance.

Defaults to 20 if not specified.

- 'expired_at': Sort by session expiration timestamp (useful for reviewing terminated sessions)

Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

Useful for security investigations when suspicious activity is traced to particular IP ranges, or for compliance requirements to identify sessions from specific geographic regions.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for retrieving a paginated list of moderator accounts.

This DTO defines the query parameters for searching and filtering moderators in the discussion board system. It supports comprehensive search capabilities including text search across usernames and emails, activity status filtering, date range queries, sorting preferences, and pagination controls.

The search functionality enables administrators to quickly locate specific moderators through partial matching on username and email fields. Activity status filtering helps distinguish between currently active moderators and those whose privileges have been revoked. Date range filters support queries like "moderators created in the last 30 days" or "moderators who haven't logged in for 90 days".

Sorting options allow organizing results by creation date, last login timestamp, or alphabetically by username, with support for both ascending and descending order. Pagination parameters ensure efficient handling of large moderator teams by limiting result set size and enabling page navigation.

All fields in this request DTO are optional, with the system applying sensible defaults when parameters are omitted. This design supports both simple browsing scenarios and complex administrative queries for moderator team analysis.

search.description:
Text search query for partial matching against moderator usernames and email addresses.

This field enables flexible discovery of moderator accounts through substring matching. The search is case-insensitive and matches against both the username and email fields of moderator records. For example, searching for "john" would match usernames like "john_smith", "johnny_admin", or emails like "john.doe@example.com".

When omitted, no text filtering is applied and all moderators matching other criteria are returned.

email.description:
Filter moderators by exact email address match.

This field allows administrators to search for a specific moderator account by their registered email address. Unlike the general search field, this performs exact matching rather than partial matching, making it ideal for precise account lookups.

The value must be a valid email address format. When specified, only moderators with this exact email address are returned.

is_active.description:
Filter moderators by account activation status.

This field enables filtering between currently active moderators and those whose privileges have been deactivated. Setting this to true returns only active moderators who can currently perform moderation duties. Setting it to false returns only inactive/deactivated moderator accounts.

When null or omitted, both active and inactive moderators are included in the results, providing a complete view of all moderator accounts regardless of status.

created_at_from.description:
Filter moderators created on or after this timestamp (inclusive).

This field supports date range queries for moderator account creation. It enables queries like "show me all moderators created in the last month" or "find moderators added after a specific date". The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z").

When specified, only moderators whose created_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are returned. When null or omitted, no lower bound is applied to the creation date filter.

created_at_to.description:
Filter moderators created on or before this timestamp (inclusive).

This field defines the upper bound for moderator account creation date queries. Combined with created_at_from, it enables precise date range filtering such as "moderators created during Q1 2024".

The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 format. When specified, only moderators whose created_at timestamp is less than or equal to this value are returned. When null or omitted, no upper bound is applied.

last_login_at_from.description:
Filter moderators who logged in on or after this timestamp (inclusive).

This field enables activity-based filtering to identify recently active moderators or track engagement patterns. It supports queries like "show moderators who have logged in within the last 7 days" or "find moderators active since the new policy was implemented".

The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 format. When specified, only moderators whose last_login_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are returned. When null or omitted, no lower bound is applied to the last login filter.

last_login_at_to.description:
Filter moderators who logged in on or before this timestamp (inclusive).

This field helps identify potentially inactive moderators by filtering for accounts that haven't logged in recently. It enables queries like "show moderators who haven't logged in for 90 days" to help administrators review and manage moderator team activity.

The timestamp must be in ISO 8601 format. When null or omitted, no upper bound is applied to the last login filter.

oneOf.description:
Field to use for sorting the moderator results.

This field determines the primary sorting criterion for the returned moderator list. The available options are:
- "created_at": Sort by account creation timestamp (useful for seeing newest or oldest moderators)
- "last_login_at": Sort by last login timestamp (useful for identifying active or inactive moderators)
- "username": Sort alphabetically by username (useful for directory-style browsing)

When omitted, the system applies a default sorting order (typically by created_at descending to show newest moderators first).

This field specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Page numbering is 1-indexed, meaning the first page is page 1, not 0.

When omitted, defaults to page 1. The total number of available pages is included in the pagination metadata of the response.

limit.description:
Number of moderator records to return per page.

This field controls the page size for pagination, determining how many moderator records are included in a single response. The value must be between 1 and 100 to ensure reasonable response sizes and system performance.

When omitted, a default limit (typically 20 or 50) is applied. Smaller limits improve response times and are suitable for UI list views, while larger limits reduce the number of requests needed to retrieve all records.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderator account.

Primary key for the moderator record. Generated automatically upon moderator account creation. Used to reference moderators in moderation logs, action attributions, and administrative operations.

email.description:
Email address for moderator authentication and communication.

Must be unique across all moderators and verified before full moderation privileges are granted. Used for authentication, password recovery, and important system notifications about moderation activities.

The email_verified field indicates whether this email address has been confirmed. Moderators with unverified emails may have restricted access to sensitive moderation functions.

username.description:
Unique username for moderator identification.

Displayed in moderation logs and when moderator edits content. Provides public identification of which moderator performed actions while maintaining email privacy.

Must be unique across all moderators to ensure clear attribution of moderation actions.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for moderator profile.

If not set, username is used for display. Allows moderators to have a more friendly or professional name shown in the interface while maintaining unique username for authentication.

Can be updated by the moderator at any time.

email_verified.description:
Whether the moderator's email address has been verified.

Must be true before granting full moderation privileges. Email verification confirms that the moderator has access to the registered email account and ensures communication channels are valid.

Verification is completed through a token-based workflow managed by the discussion_board_email_verifications table. Moderators with unverified emails may have limited access to sensitive moderation features.

email_verified_at.description:
Timestamp when email verification was completed for this moderator account.

Records the exact moment when the moderator confirmed ownership of their registered email address through the verification workflow. This timestamp provides an audit trail for email verification completion and helps track account security milestones.

Remains null until email verification is successfully completed. Once set, this value typically does not change unless the moderator changes their email address, which triggers a new verification process and updates this timestamp upon re-verification.

is_active.description:
Whether the moderator account is currently active.

Inactive moderators cannot perform moderation actions or login to the system. This flag provides administrative control over moderator access without requiring full account deletion.

Deactivation is typically used for temporary suspension of moderation privileges while maintaining the account record and associated moderation history for audit purposes.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of moderator's most recent successful login.

Tracks authentication activity for security monitoring and account activity assessment. Updated automatically each time the moderator successfully authenticates to the system. Used for activity tracking, security monitoring, and identifying inactive moderator accounts.

Remains null if the moderator has never logged in since account creation. This field helps administrators monitor moderator engagement and detect potentially compromised or abandoned accounts through unusual login patterns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was created by system administrator.

Provides audit trail for moderator account establishment and helps track account age for trust and experience assessment. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

This timestamp is immutable and set automatically upon account creation, representing when the moderator was first granted moderation privileges in the discussion board system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was last updated.

Automatically set to the current time whenever any moderator account field is modified, including profile changes, password updates, or administrative status changes. Provides audit trail for tracking account modifications and helps identify recently changed accounts.

Used for change tracking, audit logging, and detecting suspicious account modifications. Updated automatically by the system and cannot be manually set through API operations.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when moderator privileges were revoked and account deleted.

Supports soft deletion pattern, allowing moderator account records to be preserved for audit trail and historical moderation action attribution while preventing future logins and moderation activities. When set, the account is considered deleted and the moderator cannot authenticate or perform any moderation functions.

Remains null for active moderator accounts. Soft deletion preserves the complete moderation history associated with this account, ensuring transparency and accountability for past moderation decisions even after privilege revocation.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a moderator for references in moderation logs and action attributions.

Provides essential moderator identification information without exposing sensitive data like password. Used when displaying moderator information in moderation logs, recent actions, and administrative interfaces.

Includes account status fields (email_verified, is_active) to indicate the moderator's current operational state and privilege level. Contains complete timestamp information for audit trails including account creation, last activity, modifications, and soft deletion status.

email.description:
Updated email address for moderator authentication and communication.

Changing email address resets email_verified to false and triggers a new verification workflow. Must be unique across all moderators. Email format must be valid according to RFC 5322 standards.

password.description:
New password for moderator authentication (plain text, will be hashed server-side).

Must meet complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters with at least one letter and one number. The server will hash this password using bcrypt with work factor 10+ before storage. Changing password invalidates all existing authentication sessions, requiring re-login.

username.description:
Updated unique username for moderator identification.

Must be unique across all moderators. Used in moderation logs and public-facing moderation actions. Username changes are reflected in future moderation logs but do not affect historical records.

display_name.description:
Updated display name for moderator profile.

Optional friendly display name. When set to null, the system uses username for display. Can be changed freely without affecting authentication or system functionality.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IUpdate.description:
Update request for moderator account profile and authentication details.

Contains editable fields that moderators can modify in their own accounts. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates. Moderators can only update their own accounts unless they have system administrator privileges.

Critical security considerations apply to this DTO. Password changes require plain text input which is immediately hashed server-side using bcrypt. Email changes trigger re-verification workflows and reset the email_verified flag. Username changes must maintain uniqueness constraints and are reflected in future moderation actions.

System-managed fields including id, email_verified, email_verified_at, is_active, created_at, last_login_at, and deleted_at cannot be modified through this endpoint. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set by the system when changes are applied.

Validation rules enforce business constraints including email format validation (RFC 5322), username uniqueness checks, and password complexity requirements. All updates maintain referential integrity with moderation logs and authentication sessions.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for the moderator account. Auto-generated UUID that serves as the primary reference for all moderator-related operations and relationships.

email.description:
Email address for moderator authentication and communication. Must be unique across all moderators and verified.

This field is used for login credentials and system communications. Email uniqueness is enforced at the database level through a unique index.

username.description:
Unique username for moderator identification in moderation logs and actions. Displayed when moderator edits content.

The username serves as a public identifier for the moderator in system logs and moderation actions. Must be unique across all moderators and is indexed for performance.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for moderator profile. If not set, username is used for display.

Allows moderators to set a more friendly or formal display name separate from their login username. When null, the system falls back to using the username for display purposes.

email_verified.description:
Whether the moderator's email address has been verified. Must be true before granting moderation privileges.

Email verification is a critical security requirement. Moderators must verify their email address before being granted active moderation capabilities. This field is set to true only after successful email verification via the verification token workflow.

email_verified_at.description:
Timestamp when email verification was completed for this moderator account.

Records the exact moment when the moderator completed email verification. Null until verification is completed. Used for audit trails and security monitoring.

is_active.description:
Whether the moderator account is currently active. Inactive moderators cannot perform moderation actions or login.

Controls access to moderation capabilities. When set to false, the moderator is blocked from logging in and performing any moderation actions. This field is indexed for efficient filtering of active moderators.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of moderator's most recent successful login. Used for activity tracking and security monitoring.

Tracks login activity for security auditing and moderator activity monitoring. Null for accounts that have never logged in. Updated automatically on each successful authentication.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was created by system administrator.

Records when the moderator account was initially created in the system. This field is system-managed and automatically set on account creation. Used for account age tracking and audit trails.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderator account was last updated.

Automatically updated whenever any field in the moderator account is modified. Used for tracking account modifications and synchronization purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when moderator privileges were revoked and account deleted. Supports soft deletion for audit trail.

Implements soft deletion for moderator accounts. When set to a timestamp value, the account is considered deleted and the moderator loses all privileges. Null for active accounts. Preserves account records for accountability and audit purposes even after deletion.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.description:
Moderator account entity representing authenticated administrators with content moderation privileges.

Moderators are trusted users with elevated permissions to manage community content, enforce guidelines, and handle reported violations. This entity stores moderator authentication credentials, profile information, and account status. All moderation actions are logged with moderator identity for transparency and accountability.

Moderators have similar authentication requirements as regular members but with elevated access levels. They can review, edit, and remove any content on the platform, manage member accounts through suspensions and bans, and handle community reports. Moderator privileges are granted by system administrators and cannot be self-assigned.

The entity maintains comprehensive audit fields including creation timestamp, last update, last login, and soft deletion support. Email verification is required before moderators can exercise their privileges. Account status is controlled through the is_active flag, allowing temporary privilege suspension without account deletion.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for this moderator authentication session. Generated automatically when the session is created upon moderator login.

discussion_board_moderator_id.description:
Moderator who owns this authentication session.

References the moderator account that this session belongs to. Establishes the link between the session and the authenticated moderator for privilege validation and action attribution.

moderator.description:
Summary information about the moderator who owns this session.

Provides essential moderator details including username and display name for session identification and audit trail purposes. Uses summary variant to avoid excessive data in session responses.

ip.description:
IP address of the moderator's connection for this session.

Used for security monitoring and access control. Enables detection of suspicious login patterns, geographic anomalies, and unauthorized access attempts. Recorded at session creation time.

href.description:
Connection URL where the moderator session was initiated.

Typically the moderator login page or authentication endpoint. Used for tracking login source and verifying legitimate authentication flows.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating how the moderator arrived at the login page.

Provides context about the navigation path leading to authentication. Used for security analysis and understanding moderator access patterns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this moderator session was created through successful login.

Marks the beginning of the authentication session. Used to calculate session age, enforce session expiration policies, and provide audit trail for moderator access.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this session expired or was terminated.

Null for active sessions, set on logout or token expiration. Enables distinction between active and inactive sessions for security management and session cleanup. Used to enforce 30-minute access token expiration and 7-day refresh token expiration policies.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.description:
Active authentication session for a moderator enabling secure access to moderation tools.

Represents a moderator's authenticated connection to the platform. Sessions are created upon successful moderator login and used to validate moderator identity and privileges for moderation operations. Session management uses JWT tokens with 30-minute access token expiration and 7-day refresh token expiration.

Moderator sessions track connection context for security auditing and accountability. All moderation actions performed during a session can be traced back to the specific moderator and session for comprehensive audit trails.

This type is used in response bodies when returning moderator session information, such as after successful login or when listing active sessions for security monitoring.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when the total result set is divided into pages of the specified limit size. Used in conjunction with limit to implement efficient offset-based pagination.

Default value is typically 1 if not specified, returning the first page of results.

limit.description:
Number of session records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, allowing clients to balance between fewer large requests and more granular browsing. Larger limits reduce total API calls but increase response size and processing time. Smaller limits enable more responsive UI but require more requests for complete data.

Typical values range from 10-50 for user interfaces. Maximum limit of 100 prevents excessive server load from single requests.

sort.description:
Field name to sort results by, with optional direction suffix.

Specifies the sorting order for the result set. Common sort fields include 'created_at' (session creation time), 'expired_at' (session termination time), and 'ip' (IP address alphabetically).

Direction can be specified with '+' prefix for ascending or '-' prefix for descending. Examples: '-created_at' (newest first), '+ip' (IP alphabetically), 'created_at' (ascending by default).

Default sort order is typically '-created_at' to show most recent sessions first for security monitoring.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by exact IP address match.

Narrows results to only sessions that were created from the specified IP address. Used to track all login activity from a specific location, investigate suspicious access patterns, or identify concurrent sessions from the same source.

Example: '192.168.1.100' returns only sessions authenticated from that specific IP.

created_after.description:
Filter sessions created on or after this timestamp.

Returns only sessions where created_at is greater than or equal to the specified datetime. Used to define the start of a time range for security audits, activity reports, or recent session reviews.

Combine with created_before to create bounded date ranges: 'sessions created between DATE1 and DATE2'.

created_before.description:
Filter sessions created on or before this timestamp.

Returns only sessions where created_at is less than or equal to the specified datetime. Used to define the end of a time range for historical analysis or to exclude very recent sessions from reports.

Combine with created_after to create bounded date ranges for focused time period analysis.

is_active.description:
Filter sessions by active status.

When true, returns only currently active sessions (expired_at is null). When false, returns only terminated sessions (expired_at is not null). When omitted, returns all sessions regardless of status.

This filter is essential for security monitoring use cases such as identifying all currently logged-in moderators, detecting unusual concurrent sessions, or reviewing historical session activity separately from active sessions.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorSession.IReques.description:
Search, filtering, sorting, and pagination parameters for retrieving moderator authentication sessions.

This request schema enables complex queries against the moderator session dataset, supporting security monitoring workflows such as reviewing login history for specific moderators, identifying sessions from suspicious IP addresses, analyzing login patterns over time periods, and distinguishing between active and terminated sessions.

The flexible filtering options allow combining multiple criteria (IP address + date range + active status) to create precise queries for security investigations, compliance audits, or operational reporting. Pagination and sorting controls enable efficient browsing of large session datasets while maintaining responsive API performance.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for this moderation log entry. Auto-generated when the moderation action is recorded and used for retrieving specific log entries from the audit trail.

discussion_board_moderator_id.description:
Moderator who performed this moderation action.

References discussion_board_moderators.id to establish accountability for this specific moderation decision. Critical for audit trail integrity and tracking which moderator took what actions.

moderator.description:
Summary information about the moderator who performed this action.

Provides moderator username and identification for audit trail transparency. Enables quick identification of which moderator took this action without requiring additional API calls.

action_type.description:
Type of moderation action performed.

Valid values: 'article_edited' (moderator edited article content), 'article_deleted' (moderator removed article), 'attachment_removed' (moderator deleted specific attachment), 'account_suspended' (member account temporarily suspended), 'account_banned' (member account permanently banned), 'account_restored' (suspension or ban reversed). Categorizes the moderation action for filtering and analysis.

reason.description:
Moderator's documented explanation for taking this action.

Required for all moderation actions to ensure accountability and transparency. Examples: 'Removed spam content', 'Suspended for harassment', 'Edited to remove personal information'. Provides context for why this moderation decision was made.

action_details.description:
Additional contextual details about the moderation action.

May include what was changed in an edit, which attachment was removed, or specific policy violations cited. Provides complete context for the audit trail beyond the basic reason field.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Article that was moderated (edited, deleted, or had attachments removed).

Null if action was user account management rather than content moderation. References discussion_board_articles.id to link this log entry to the affected content.

article.description:
Summary information about the article that was moderated.

Provides article title and basic context for content moderation actions. Null if this log entry records account management actions rather than content moderation.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Member whose account was affected by moderator action.

Null if action was content moderation rather than account management. References discussion_board_members.id for account suspensions, bans, or restorations.

affectedMember.description:
Summary information about the member whose account was affected.

Provides member username and profile information for account management actions (suspension, ban, restoration). Null if this log entry records content moderation rather than account actions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderation action was performed.

Used for chronological audit trail ordering, moderation activity reporting, and tracking response times. Immutable once recorded to maintain audit trail integrity.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.description:
Comprehensive audit trail entry recording a specific moderator action for accountability and transparency.

Records every content moderation and user management action taken by moderators, including article edits, article deletions, attachment removals, account suspensions, and account bans. Each log entry captures what action was taken, which moderator performed it, what content or user was affected, when it occurred, and the moderator's documented reason.

The moderation log serves multiple critical purposes: accountability (tracking who did what and why), transparency (allowing review of moderation decisions), dispute resolution (providing evidence for appeals), and pattern analysis (identifying problematic content or users requiring escalated action).

Log entries are immutable and retained indefinitely per business requirements. Moderators and administrators can search and filter logs by action type, moderator, affected content, affected user, or time period to review moderation history, investigate specific incidents, or generate moderation activity reports.

This comprehensive audit trail ensures moderation decisions are documented, reviewable, and consistent with community guidelines.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the moderation logs list.

Provides information about total record count, current page number, page size, and total pages. Enables efficient navigation through potentially large moderation log histories.

data.description:
Array of moderation log summary entries for the current page.

Contains the actual moderation log records matching the query criteria. Each entry provides essential information about a moderation action for display in audit logs and moderation activity dashboards.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.ISummary.description:
Paginated collection of moderation log summaries.

Used for displaying moderation activity lists with pagination support. Allows administrators and moderators to review moderation history, filter by action type, moderator, or time period, and navigate through results efficiently.

Supports audit trails, accountability reviews, and moderation pattern analysis.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering moderation history.

This DTO enables moderators to query the comprehensive moderation log with flexible filtering, sorting, and pagination. It supports filtering by action type (article edits, deletions, suspensions, bans), date ranges, specific moderators, and affected entities. The request structure facilitates complex queries like "Show me all article deletions by moderator X in the past 30 days" or "Find all suspension actions against member Y".

The filtering capabilities enable moderators to investigate specific incidents, generate enforcement reports, identify moderation patterns, and review team member activity. Combined with pagination, this ensures efficient retrieval even when querying extensive moderation histories spanning months or years.

All timestamp filters use ISO 8601 datetime format for consistency. Action type filters accept predefined values matching the action_type field in discussion_board_moderation_logs (article_edited, article_deleted, attachment_removed, account_suspended, account_banned, account_restored).

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting from 1. Used to retrieve specific result pages when the total moderation log entries exceed the limit per page.

limit.description: Number of moderation log entries to return per page. Maximum 100 entries to ensure reasonable response sizes. Default is typically 20 entries per page.

action_types.description: Filter by specific moderation action types. Valid values: 'article_edited', 'article_deleted', 'attachment_removed', 'account_suspended', 'account_banned', 'account_restored'. When specified, only log entries matching these action types are returned. Omit to include all action types.

moderator_id.description: Filter by specific moderator who performed the actions. When specified, only shows moderation actions taken by this moderator. Useful for reviewing individual moderator activity or auditing specific moderator decisions.

from_date.description: Start of date range filter (inclusive). Only returns moderation actions performed on or after this timestamp. ISO 8601 datetime format. Useful for reviewing recent activity or specific time periods.

to_date.description: End of date range filter (inclusive). Only returns moderation actions performed on or before this timestamp. ISO 8601 datetime format. Combined with from_date, enables precise time range queries.

article_id.description: Filter by specific article that was moderated. Returns only moderation actions affecting this article (edits, deletions, attachment removals). Useful for reviewing the complete moderation history of a specific piece of content.

member_id.description: Filter by specific member affected by moderation actions. Returns account-level actions (suspensions, bans, restorations) targeting this member. Useful for reviewing enforcement history before applying additional disciplinary actions.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Valid values: 'created_at' (sort by action timestamp), 'action_type' (group by action type). Default is 'created_at' for chronological ordering.
Field to sort results by. Valid values: 'created_at' (sort by action timestamp), 'action_type' (group by action type). Default is 'created_at' for chronological ordering.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Valid values: 'created_at' (sort by action timestamp), 'action_type' (group by action type). Default is 'created_at' for chronological ordering.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is 'desc' to show most recent moderation actions first.
Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is 'desc' to show most recent moderation actions first.

order.description: Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending (oldest first), 'desc' for descending (newest first). Default is 'desc' to show most recent moderation actions first.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for this guest tracking record. Used internally for analytics and conversion tracking.

session_identifier.description:
Unique session identifier for tracking guest browsing activity.

Generated on first visit and stored in browser. Enables tracking of guest behavior across multiple visits without requiring authentication or personal information. Used for analytics and conversion funnel analysis.

first_visit_at.description:
Timestamp of the guest's first visit to the platform.

Used to calculate visitor recency and lifetime. Helps identify new versus returning guests for engagement analysis.

last_visit_at.description:
Timestamp of the guest's most recent visit.

Updated on each session to track engagement frequency. Enables calculation of time since last visit and identification of active versus dormant guests.

page_views.description:
Total number of page views by this guest across all visits.

Indicates engagement level and content consumption. Higher page views suggest greater interest in the platform and higher conversion potential.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest record was created in the system.

Corresponds to the moment when the guest's first session was initialized and tracking began. This field matches the created_at column from the discussion_board_guests Prisma schema.

Used for analytics record keeping, data lifecycle management, and understanding the age of guest tracking data. Typically identical or very close to first_visit_at for normal operation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest record was last modified in the database.

Corresponds to the updated_at column from the discussion_board_guests Prisma schema. Updated whenever any field in the guest record changes, such as incrementing page_views or updating last_visit_at.

Useful for data freshness validation, understanding recent activity patterns, and cache invalidation logic. In active sessions, this will be updated frequently as the guest browses content.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an unauthenticated visitor for analytics and tracking contexts.

Provides essential guest identification and engagement metrics without exposing technical implementation details like IP addresses or user agent strings. Used in analytics dashboards, conversion reports, and traffic analysis.

This lightweight variant focuses on visitor identity and engagement metrics. Excludes sensitive tracking details like IP address and user agent that are only needed for internal security monitoring.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Combined with limit to calculate result offset. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Maximum number of guest records to return per page.

Controls page size for pagination, with allowed range from 1 to 100 records. Lower limits improve response times for quick scans, while higher limits reduce total request count for bulk analysis. Defaults to a sensible value (typically 20-50) if not specified.

search.description:
General search term for filtering guest records across multiple fields.

Searches across session_identifier, ip_address, and user_agent fields using partial matching. Enables administrators to quickly locate specific guest sessions by any known identifier or characteristic.

Example: Searching '192.168' finds all guests from that IP range, while 'Chrome' finds all Chrome browser users.

ip_address.description:
Filter guest records by exact or partial IP address match.

Supports both exact IP matching (e.g., '192.168.1.100') and prefix-based filtering (e.g., '192.168' to find all guests from that subnet). Used for security analysis, geographic traffic patterns, and abuse investigation.

user_agent_contains.description:
Filter guest records by user agent string containing specified text.

Performs case-insensitive substring matching against the user_agent field. Useful for finding all guests using specific browsers, operating systems, or device types.

Examples: 'Mobile' finds mobile devices, 'Windows' finds Windows users, 'Safari' finds Safari browsers.

first_visit_from.description:
Filter guests whose first visit occurred on or after this date.

Defines the start of the first visit date range for filtering new visitor acquisition. Combined with first_visit_to to analyze visitor acquisition within specific timeframes.

ISO 8601 format with timezone. Example: '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z' for visitors acquired since January 2024.

first_visit_to.description:
Filter guests whose first visit occurred on or before this date.

Defines the end of the first visit date range. Used with first_visit_from to analyze visitor acquisition patterns within specific periods.

ISO 8601 format with timezone. Example: '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z' for visitors acquired through end of 2024.

last_visit_from.description:
Filter guests whose last visit occurred on or after this date.

Identifies recently active guests by setting a minimum last visit threshold. Useful for finding currently engaged visitors or calculating active visitor counts within recent timeframes.

Example: Setting to 7 days ago finds all guests active within the past week.

last_visit_to.description:
Filter guests whose last visit occurred on or before this date.

Identifies dormant or inactive guests by setting a maximum last visit threshold. Combined with last_visit_from to analyze visitor retention patterns or identify guests who may have abandoned the platform.

Example: Setting to 30 days ago finds guests who haven't visited in over a month.

min_page_views.description:
Filter guests with at least this many total page views.

Sets a minimum engagement threshold to identify highly engaged visitors. Higher values filter for power users who demonstrate strong interest and may be prime conversion candidates for member registration.

Example: Setting to 50 finds guests who have viewed at least 50 pages, indicating substantial platform engagement.

max_page_views.description:
Filter guests with at most this many total page views.

Sets a maximum engagement threshold, useful for identifying low-engagement or new visitors. Can be combined with min_page_views to analyze specific engagement tiers.

Example: Setting to 5 finds guests with minimal exploration, potentially indicating unclear value proposition or poor initial experience.

oneOf.description:
Field name to sort guest records by.

Determines the ordering dimension for results. Common use cases:
- 'page_views': Rank by engagement level (most to least engaged)
- 'last_visit_at': Show most recently active guests first
- 'first_visit_at': Analyze by visitor acquisition timeline
- 'created_at': Database insertion order

Defaults to a sensible ordering (typically 'last_visit_at' descending) if not specified.

Determines the ordering dimension for results. Common use cases:
- 'page_views': Rank by engagement level (most to least engaged)
- 'last_visit_at': Show most recently active guests first
- 'first_visit_at': Analyze by visitor acquisition timeline
- 'created_at': Database insertion order

Defaults to a sensible ordering (typically 'last_visit_at' descending) if not specified.

Contains the essential information moderators must provide when applying disciplinary measures for policy violations. The moderator specifies the target member, chooses between temporary suspension or permanent ban, documents the violation reason, and sets the duration for suspensions.

id.description:

Used for referencing specific attachments in API operations, download URLs, and deletion requests.

discussion_board_article_id.description:

References the discussion_board_articles table. Each attachment is permanently associated with exactly one article. When the article is deleted, all its attachments are cascade deleted to maintain referential integrity.

discussion_board_member_id.description:

Foreign key referencing discussion_board_members table. Provides attribution for the attachment upload and enables audit trails. type.description:

Valid values are 'image' for visual content (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) or 'file' for documents (PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, TXT, CSV). This discriminator determines size limits (images: 5MB max, documents: 10MB max) and display handling. Used for validation during upload and proper rendering in the UI.

format.description:
File format extension indicating the specific attachment format.

Examples include 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp' for images, and 'pdf', 'doc', 'docx', 'xls', 'xlsx', 'txt', 'csv' for documents. This field is used for validation against allowed formats, determining the appropriate MIME type for downloads, and displaying file type icons in the user interface.

size.description:
File size in bytes representing the storage space consumed by this attachment.

Used to enforce size limits during upload (images: 5MB max, documents: 10MB max, total per article: 25MB max). Also displayed to users in human-readable format (KB, MB) to help them understand file sizes before downloading. Essential for storage quota management and bandwidth planning.

original_filename.description:

This is the filename the user sees when viewing attachments and the suggested filename when downloading. Maximum 255 characters to comply with filesystem limitations. The system sanitizes this filename to remove potentially dangerous characters while preserving readability.

storage_path.description:

Used by the application backend to retrieve and serve file content. This path references the actual file in the storage system (local filesystem, S3, CDN, etc.) and is not exposed to end users. Contains the unique storage identifier to prevent filename collisions and enable efficient file retrieval.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded and created in the system.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone. Used for displaying upload time to users, sorting attachments chronologically, and tracking content creation patterns. This timestamp is immutable after creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last modification to the attachment record metadata.

Updated automatically when attachment metadata changes (such as filename updates). Recorded in ISO 8601 format. Note that file content itself is immutable - if the file needs to change, a new attachment must be created.

deleted_at.description:

After the retention period expires, soft-deleted attachments are permanently removed from storage and the database.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.description:
Complete attachment record representing an image or document file associated with a discussion board article.

Attachments support discussion articles with visual evidence, charts, documents, and reference materials. Each attachment belongs to exactly one article and is uploaded by a specific member during article creation or editing.

The system supports two attachment types: images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP up to 5MB, maximum 10 per article) and documents (PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, TXT, CSV up to 10MB, maximum 5 per article). The combined total attachment size per article cannot exceed 25MB.

Attachments undergo security validation including file type verification by examining content headers, malware scanning, and metadata stripping to protect user privacy. The system generates unique storage paths and sanitizes filenames to prevent security vulnerabilities.

Attachments are managed exclusively through their parent articles. When articles are deleted, all associated attachments are cascade deleted. The type field discriminates between image and file attachments, while format specifies the exact file format. Size and original filename are preserved for display and download purposes. Soft deletion is supported to enable recovery if needed.

type.description:
Attachment type discriminator indicating whether this is an image or document file.

Must be 'image' for visual content (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) or 'file' for documents (PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, TXT, CSV). This determines the size limit (images: 5MB max, documents: 10MB max) and quantity limit (images: 10 max per article, documents: 5 max per article) that will be enforced during validation.

format.description:
File format extension for validation and MIME type determination.

Examples: 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'pdf', 'doc', 'docx', 'xls', 'xlsx', 'txt', 'csv'. Must match the actual file content type for security validation. The system validates this against the file content headers to prevent type spoofing attacks.

size.description:
File size in bytes for validation against size limits.

Must not exceed 5MB (5,242,880 bytes) for images or 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) for documents. The system validates that the total size of all attachments for the article does not exceed 25MB. This field must accurately reflect the actual file size to ensure proper quota enforcement.

original_filename.description:
Original filename from the user's upload to preserve for display and download.

Maximum 255 characters. This filename will be shown to users viewing the attachment and used as the suggested download filename. The system sanitizes this value to remove potentially dangerous characters while preserving readability.

storage_path.description:
Pre-uploaded file URL or storage reference where the file content has been stored.

Following the URL-only file upload pattern, files must be uploaded to the storage system first (via a separate file upload endpoint), and this field contains the resulting storage path or URL. The system uses this path to access the file content for serving downloads and generating thumbnails.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ICreat.description:
Request body for creating a new attachment associated with a discussion board article.

This DTO follows the two-phase file upload pattern where files are first uploaded to storage (obtaining a storage_path/URL), then the attachment metadata is submitted to create the attachment record.

Validation enforces attachment type restrictions (image vs document), format allowlists (JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP for images, PDF/DOC/DOCX/XLS/XLSX/TXT/CSV for documents), size limits (5MB for images, 10MB for documents), quantity limits (10 images and 5 documents per article), and total size limit (25MB per article).

Security validation includes file type verification by examining content headers (not just extensions), malware scanning, and metadata stripping to protect privacy. The discussion_board_article_id is provided via the path parameter, not in the request body. The discussion_board_member_id is automatically populated from the authenticated user's JWT token.

max_size.description:

When specified, returns only attachments with size less than or equal to this value. Combined with min_size enables size range filtering. When null or omitted, no maximum size restriction is applied.

When specified, returns only attachments whose original_filename contains this search term (case-insensitive substring match). Useful for finding specific supporting materials within articles that have multiple attachments. When null or omitted, no filename filtering is applied.

When specified, returns only attachments with created_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime. Combined with uploaded_after enables date range filtering. When null or omitted, no end date restriction is applied.

sort_by.description:

Specify 'created_at' for chronological sorting by upload timestamp, 'size' for sorting by file size, or 'filename' for alphabetical sorting by original_filename. When null or omitted, defaults to 'created_at' sorting.

sort_order.description:

Specify 'asc' for ascending order (oldest first, smallest first, or A-Z) or 'desc' for descending order (newest first, largest first, or Z-A). When null or omitted, defaults to 'desc' (most recently uploaded first).

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IReque.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering attachment listings with pagination and sorting.

Provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for retrieving attachments associated with a specific article. All parameters are optional, allowing flexible queries from simple paginated lists to complex filtered searches. When no filters are specified, returns all attachments for the article in default sort order (most recently uploaded first).

Supports filtering by attachment characteristics including type (image vs document), specific format (file extension), file size ranges, original filename text search, and upload date ranges. Multiple filters can be combined to narrow results precisely, such as finding all PDF documents over 1MB uploaded in the last month.

Sorting options enable ordering by upload date (chronological), file size (largest or smallest first), or filename (alphabetical). Combined with the sort direction parameter, this provides full control over result ordering to match different use cases like finding the most recent attachments or the largest files.

Pagination parameters control the number of results per page and which page to retrieve, ensuring efficient loading for articles with many attachments. The limit parameter is capped at 100 to prevent excessive memory usage while allowing sufficient flexibility for different UI requirements.

IDiscussionBoardContentReport.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering content reports.

Supports comprehensive filtering capabilities including pagination, status filtering, category filtering, article-specific filtering, member-specific filtering, moderator-specific filtering, and date range queries for both submission and resolution timestamps.

All parameters are optional with sensible defaults optimized for moderation workflows. Default behavior (no filters) returns all reports paginated by submission date (oldest first), which surfaces the most urgent pending reports requiring moderator attention.

Multiple filters can be combined to create highly specific queries, such as 'pending spam reports from the last week' or 'reports resolved by a specific moderator in the past month'.

id.description:
Primary identifier for the content report.

Unique identifier (UUID format) used to track and reference this specific report throughout its lifecycle from submission through resolution.

This ID is used in moderation operations to update report status, add resolution notes, and track moderator actions in audit logs.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Reported article that allegedly violates community guidelines.

References the discussion_board_articles.id of the article being reported. This foreign key establishes the relationship between reports and the content they flag.

Multiple members can report the same article independently, with each creating a separate report record. Moderators use this field to identify which article requires review and to view all reports submitted against a particular piece of content.

discussion_board_member_id.description:
Member who submitted this content report.

References discussion_board_members.id of the reporting member. This establishes accountability and enables moderators to track reporting patterns.

The reporting member's identity is visible to moderators to help identify potential abuse of the reporting system (e.g., targeted harassment through false reports) while maintaining appropriate confidentiality from article authors to encourage honest community moderation.

oneOf.description:

Tracking the resolver enables accountability, workload distribution analysis, and moderator performance metrics. It also provides context for resolution decisions in case of appeals or questions about moderation actions.

IDiscussionBoardModerationDashboard.description:
Real-time moderation dashboard overview with key metrics and pending tasks.

This computed DTO aggregates data from multiple tables to provide moderators with an at-a-glance view of platform health, pending work, and recent enforcement activity. It combines counts, statistics, and summaries from discussion_board_content_reports (pending reports needing review), discussion_board_articles (recently published content), discussion_board_account_actions (active suspensions and bans), and discussion_board_moderation_logs (recent moderator activity across the team).

The dashboard serves as the entry point for moderators' daily workflow, helping them prioritize tasks based on urgency and volume. High pending report counts signal backlog requiring immediate attention, while low recent activity combined with growing content volume may indicate need for additional moderator resources. The recent actions summary provides team-wide visibility into enforcement patterns and workload distribution.

This is not a persistent entity but rather a computed aggregation response. The data is calculated on-demand when moderators access the dashboard, ensuring real-time accuracy. All counts and statistics reflect current database state at the moment of request.

pending_reports_count.description: Number of content reports submitted by members that are currently pending moderator review (status='pending'). Indicates backlog of flagged content requiring attention. High counts signal need for immediate moderator action.

flagged_articles_count.description: Number of published articles that have received multiple content reports or are flagged for immediate review. Represents content with community concerns requiring moderator judgment and potential action.

active_suspensions_count.description: Number of member accounts currently suspended or banned (status='active' in account_actions). Indicates current enforcement level and members blocked from platform access. Includes both temporary suspensions and permanent bans.

recent_moderation_actions_count.description: Number of moderation actions performed by all moderators in the past 24 hours. Provides visibility into team-wide enforcement activity level. Includes content moderation (edits, deletions) and account actions (suspensions, bans).

recent_moderation_actions.description: Most recent moderation actions taken by any moderator in the past 24 hours, limited to 10 entries. Provides quick overview of recent enforcement activity for team coordination and pattern awareness. Sorted by timestamp descending (newest first).

recent_published_articles_count.description: Number of articles published in the past 24 hours. Indicates content creation velocity and potential need for quality review. High publication rates may require additional moderator attention to ensure content quality.

average_response_time_hours.description:
Average time in hours from report submission to moderator resolution.

Calculated by averaging the time difference between created_at and resolved_at timestamps across all resolved content reports. This metric provides insight into typical moderation response speed and helps track whether moderators are meeting response time targets defined in success metrics.

A lower value indicates faster moderation response, which correlates with better community trust and content quality maintenance.

median_response_time_hours.description:
Median response time in hours representing the 50th percentile.

The median provides a more robust measure of typical response time compared to average, as it is not skewed by outliers. Half of all reports are resolved faster than this value, and half take longer.

Useful for understanding the central tendency of moderation response times without being affected by occasional very fast or very slow resolutions.

percentile_90_response_time_hours.description:
90th percentile response time in hours identifying outlier cases.

90% of reports are resolved within this timeframe, while 10% take longer. This metric helps identify the upper boundary of normal response times and highlights cases that may require process improvements or additional resources.

High 90th percentile values relative to median suggest significant variability in response times or systematic delays for certain report types.

percentage_resolved_within_24_hours.description:
Percentage of reports resolved within 24 hours of submission.

This metric directly measures performance against common moderation SLA targets. Many platforms aim for 24-hour response times for community-submitted reports as a best practice.

Higher percentages indicate more responsive moderation and better alignment with platform success criteria for timely content review.

percentage_resolved_within_7_days.description:
Percentage of reports resolved within 7 days of submission.

Provides a broader view of moderation coverage, capturing nearly all resolved reports under normal operating conditions. Reports taking longer than 7 days may indicate edge cases, complex investigations, or resource constraints.

This extended timeframe metric complements the 24-hour metric to show overall resolution coverage.

total_pending_reports.description:
Current count of unresolved reports awaiting moderator review.

Represents the backlog of content reports that have been submitted but not yet acted upon by moderators. A growing backlog may indicate insufficient moderation capacity or increasing report volume.

This real-time metric helps administrators monitor moderation workload and resource allocation needs.

response_times_by_category.description:
Breakdown of response time statistics by report category.

Analyzes whether certain violation types (Spam, Offensive Content, Misinformation, Off-Topic, Other) receive faster or slower moderation attention. This categorical analysis helps identify if resource allocation matches the severity and volume patterns of different report types.

Enables administrators to optimize moderation workflows by understanding which categories may need priority handling or additional specialized resources.

IDiscussionBoardModerationResponseTimeSt.description:
Statistical summary of moderation response time performance metrics.

Provides comprehensive analytics on how quickly moderators review and resolve community-submitted content reports. This response type supports the success metrics tracking requirements defined in the business documentation, enabling data-driven assessment of moderation team performance.

The statistics include multiple indicators: average and median response times for understanding typical performance, 90th percentile for identifying outliers, resolution percentages within target timeframes (24 hours and 7 days) for SLA tracking, current pending report count for workload monitoring, and category-specific breakdowns for identifying optimization opportunities.

This is aggregated, read-only statistical data computed from the discussion_board_content_reports table. It does not expose individual reporter identities or specific report details, maintaining privacy while providing actionable performance insights.

Platform administrators and moderators use these metrics to ensure response time targets are being met, identify areas requiring additional resources or process improvements, and track moderation team effectiveness over time.

Provides volume context for the response time statistics. A category with very few reports may show unreliable average times due to small sample size, while high-volume categories provide more statistically significant performance indicators.

IDiscussionBoardModerationResponseTimeBy.description:

Represents performance metrics for a specific violation category, enabling analysis of whether different report types receive different levels of moderation attention. This granular breakdown helps identify if certain categories are under-resourced or over-prioritized relative to their volume and importance.

By comparing response times across categories, administrators can optimize moderation workflows to ensure appropriate prioritization based on severity, implement specialized training for complex categories, and balance workload distribution among moderation team members.

start_date.description:
Start of the date range for filtering moderation actions (inclusive).

Specifies the earliest timestamp for moderation actions to include in statistics. Only actions with created_at >= start_date are counted. When omitted, statistics include all actions from the beginning of recorded moderation history.

Used to focus analysis on recent activity, specific time periods, or to compare moderation patterns across different date ranges. Combined with end_date to define precise analytical windows for trend analysis and reporting.

end_date.description:
End of the date range for filtering moderation actions (inclusive).

Specifies the latest timestamp for moderation actions to include in statistics. Only actions with created_at <= end_date are counted. When omitted, statistics include all actions up to the current time.

Enables historical analysis, period-over-period comparisons, and focused reporting on specific timeframes. Combined with start_date to create bounded analytical windows for measuring moderation activity trends.

moderator_ids.description:
Optional filter to limit statistics to actions performed by specific moderators.

Array of moderator UUIDs ({@link discussion_board_moderators.id}) to include in the analysis. When provided, only moderation actions performed by these moderators are counted. When omitted, statistics include actions from all moderators.

Enables workload analysis for individual moderators or moderator teams, comparison of moderation patterns across different moderators, and assessment of moderator activity levels. Useful for performance evaluation, training needs identification, and understanding moderation style variations.

action_types.description:
Optional filter to limit statistics to specific types of moderation actions.

Array of action type values to include in the analysis. Valid values match the action_type field from discussion_board_moderation_logs. When provided, only these action types are included in results. When omitted, statistics cover all action types.

Enables focused analysis on specific enforcement categories (e.g., only content moderation actions, only account management actions). Useful for policy-specific reporting, trend analysis of particular violation types, and targeted moderation process improvement.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatisticsByTy.description:
Filter criteria for retrieving moderation action statistics grouped by action type.

Defines the parameters for aggregating and filtering moderation log data to produce actionable analytics. All properties are optional, allowing flexible queries from broad platform-wide statistics to highly targeted analysis of specific moderators, time periods, or action categories.

This request type supports complex analytical scenarios including trend analysis over time (using date filters), moderator workload assessment (using moderator_ids), policy enforcement pattern analysis (using action_types), and comprehensive platform health monitoring (using no filters for system-wide metrics).

The filtering logic applies AND semantics across different filter types (date range AND moderator list AND action types), enabling precise control over the statistical scope while maintaining query simplicity and performance.

statistics.description:
Array of statistical records, one for each moderation action type, containing aggregated counts and trend data.

Each statistic represents a distinct action type (article_edited, article_deleted, attachment_removed, account_suspended, account_banned, account_restored) with its corresponding activity metrics. The array enables comparison across different moderation action categories to identify patterns, high-volume actions, and enforcement trends.

Statistics are computed from the discussion_board_moderation_logs table using GROUP BY action_type aggregations, filtered according to the request criteria (date range, moderators, action types). Empty array returned when no moderation actions match the specified filters.

total_actions.description:
Total count of all moderation actions across all action types within the filtered period.

Represents the sum of action_count values across all statistics entries. This aggregate metric provides an overall measure of moderation activity volume, enabling workload assessment and capacity planning.

Used to calculate percentage distributions for each action type and to normalize trend comparisons across different time periods or moderator subsets.

date_range.description:
Actual date range covered by the returned statistics, reflecting the applied filters or system data boundaries.

May differ from the requested date range if no data exists for the full period or if request omitted date filters (defaults to system-wide date range). Provides context for interpreting the statistical results and ensures consumers understand the temporal scope of the metrics.

IDiscussionBoardModerationStatisticsByTy.description:
Aggregated moderation action statistics grouped by action type for analytical insights and reporting.

Provides comprehensive analytics on moderation activity patterns by categorizing and counting actions according to their type (content edits, deletions, attachment removals, account suspensions, bans, and restorations). This response enables moderators and administrators to understand enforcement patterns, identify high-volume action types, assess moderation workload distribution, and track community health indicators.

The statistics support data-driven decision-making about moderation policies, resource allocation, and guideline enforcement consistency. By analyzing action type distributions and trends, platform administrators can detect anomalies, measure moderation team performance, and identify areas requiring additional moderator training or policy clarification.

This type is returned by the moderation statistics endpoint and aggregates data from the discussion_board_moderation_logs table. It implements the Success Metrics requirements for measuring moderation activity rates and content quality indicators through quantitative analysis of logged moderation actions.

Total number of moderation actions of this type within the filtered period.

Aggregate count computed from discussion_board_moderation_logs WHERE action_type = this type AND other filter criteria. Represents the volume of this specific enforcement action, indicating how frequently moderators use this action type.

High counts may indicate systemic content quality issues, guideline violations, or areas where community education could reduce moderation burden. Comparing counts across action types reveals enforcement priorities and community behavior patterns.

percentage.description:
Percentage of total moderation actions represented by this action type.

Calculated as (action_count / total_actions) * 100, where total_actions is the sum across all action types. Provides normalized comparison enabling identification of dominant action types regardless of absolute volume changes.

Percentage distribution reveals moderation focus areas, policy enforcement balance, and relative frequency of different violation types. Shifts in percentage over time indicate changing community dynamics or moderation policy adjustments.

start_date.description:

Represents the earliest timestamp included in the range. All data points with timestamps >= start_date fall within this range. Used to define temporal boundaries for filtering, aggregation, and analysis operations.

In statistical contexts, this reflects the actual start of the data included in results, which may differ from requested start_date if no data exists before a certain point or if request omitted the filter.

IDateRange.description:

Represents an inclusive interval [start_date, end_date] used for filtering time-series data, defining analytical windows, and communicating the temporal scope of results. Both boundaries are inclusive, meaning data points exactly matching the boundary timestamps are included in the range.

This reusable type supports various temporal operations including historical analysis, trend comparison, period-over-period metrics, and time-bounded reporting. It provides clear semantic meaning for date range parameters and ensures consistent temporal boundary handling across the API.
